<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915617_theRebbe_822" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915617_theRebbe_822__p004">
  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that Chochmah's state of being "Ayin" relative to Binah is only from the perspective of its role as a source, while the essence of Chochmah itself is "Yesh," and this distinction parallels the difference between lower Daat and upper Daat, with further gradations within Chochmah itself.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And the explanation is,</t>
    <t s="1">that this [fact] that Chochmah is Ayin,</t>
    <t s="2">is like [the fact] that it becomes a source for Binah,</t>
    <t s="3">for since the coming-into-being of Binah from Chochmah is through Chochmah being concealed from Binah,</t>
    <t s="4">therefore it is then called by the name Ayin</t>
    <t s="5">(that which is not grasped).</t>
    <t s="6">But the essence of Chochmah itself is in the category of Yesh,</t>
    <t s="7">and this [fact] that Chochmah is a source for Binah</t>
    <t s="8">(and all the more so Binah itself)</t>
    <t s="9">is Ayin relative to the essence of Chochmah,</t>
    <t s="10">an Ayin that is considered as nothing.</t>
    <t s="11">And based on this,</t>
    <t s="12">in the aspect of Chochmah that becomes a source for Binah – it is analogous to the knowledge of lower Daat, where above is Ayin and below is Yesh,</t>
    <t s="13">and in the aspect of the essence of Chochmah that is above the source for Binah – it is analogous to the knowledge of upper Daat, where above is Yesh and below is Ayin.</t>
    <t s="14">[And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="15">that also in Chochmah that is above the source for Binah there are two levels.</t>
    <t s="16">The essence of Chochmah and the illumination of Chochmah.</t>
    <t s="17">For this matter that is in Chochmah</t>
    <t s="18">(the feeling that the source for Binah is an Ayin that is considered as nothing)</t>
    <t s="19">is the illumination of Chochmah and not its essence,</t>
    <t s="20">except that this illumination is attached to the essence,</t>
    <t s="21">and therefore it is felt in it that all matters that are not the essence of Chochmah</t>
    <t s="22">are considered as nothing.</t>
    <t s="23">For the illumination of Chochmah that becomes a source for Binah is a distinct illumination,</t>
    <t s="24">and therefore it is a source for Binah – analogous to the Ayin of created Yesh,</t>
    <t s="25">and the illumination of Chochmah that is attached to the essence of Chochmah,</t>
    <t s="26">it is felt in it that it is an Ayin that is considered as nothing relative to the essence of Chochmah – analogous to the Ayin of true Yesh].</t>
    <t s="27">And from the distinctions between the internal union of Chochmah and Binah and the external union of Chochmah and Binah is,</t>
    <t s="28">that in the external union the drawing down is from the externality of Chochmah,</t>
    <t s="29">that is, from the aspect of Chochmah as it becomes a source for Binah</t>
    <t s="30">(and even this aspect of Chochmah is concealed from Binah,</t>
    <t s="31">an Ayin that is not grasped),</t>
    <t s="32">and in the internal union the drawing down is from the innerness of Chochmah,</t>
    <t s="33">and this drawing down is in revelation within Binah,</t>
    <t s="34">and since relative to the innerness of Chochmah the source for Binah and all the more so Binah itself are considered as nothing,</t>
    <t s="35">therefore,</t>
    <t s="36">through the innerness of Chochmah being revealed in Binah,</t>
    <t s="37">it [Binah] is included in Chochmah.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section clarifies that the "Yesh" and "Ayin" within Chochmah itself relate to the true Yesh of Ein Sof and the Ayin of created Yesh, and that the distinction between upper and lower Daat applies specifically to the internal and external unions of Chochmah and Binah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">And behold, this that was explained above, that the essence of Chochmah is Yesh and the illumination of Chochmah is an Ayin that is considered as nothing relative to the essence of Chochmah,</t>
    <t s="2">they are the two matters of Yesh and Ayin that are in Chochmah itself,</t>
    <t s="3">but in generality,</t>
    <t s="4">the matter of Yesh that is in Chochmah is that in Chochmah dwells the Ein Sof, the true Yesh,</t>
    <t s="5">and the Ayin that is in Chochmah is,</t>
    <t s="6">that the entirety of Chochmah</t>
    <t s="7">(also the essence of Chochmah)</t>
    <t s="8">is in self-nullification to the Ein Sof, in that it is felt in it that above is Yesh and below is Ayin,</t>
    <t s="9">and it is the Ayin of true Yesh.</t>
    <t s="10">But this [fact] that Chochmah becomes a source for Binah is the Ayin of created Yesh.</t>
    <t s="11">And based on this,</t>
    <t s="12">this [fact] that in the external union of Chochmah and Binah it is lower Daat,</t>
    <t s="13">is also from the side of Chochmah.</t>
    <t s="14">For this that was explained above</t>
    <t s="15">(section 3)</t>
    <t s="16">that in Chochmah there is upper Daat</t>
    <t s="17">(and specifically in Binah there is lower Daat, because only the intellect of Chochmah is drawn into Binah)</t>
    <t s="18">is in generality,</t>
    <t s="19">but in particularity,</t>
    <t s="20">the matter of lower Daat that is in the external union of Chochmah and Binah is also from the side of Chochmah,</t>
    <t s="21">since Chochmah</t>
    <t s="22">(in the external union)</t>
    <t s="23">is the Ayin of created Yesh,</t>
    <t s="24">and the main matter of upper Daat is in the internal union of Chochmah and Binah,</t>
    <t s="25">for Chochmah</t>
    <t s="26">(that is in this union)</t>
    <t s="27">is the Ayin of true Yesh,</t>
    <t s="28">and also Binah is included in Chochmah.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section applies the previous concepts to explain the blessing "Blessed is He who performed miracles for our fathers" (in plural), indicating that the elevation from which miracles are drawn is also within Chochmah, from its essence above its role as a source for Binah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And based on this we can explain what is said, "Blessed is He who performed miracles for our fathers"</t>
    <t s="1">(in the plural),</t>
    <t s="2">that the elevation and ascent</t>
    <t s="3">(from which the miracles are drawn)</t>
    <t s="4">is also in Chochmah,</t>
    <t s="5">for Chochmah, from its own side</t>
    <t s="6">(as it is in the external union)</t>
    <t s="7">is a source for Binah – the Ayin of created Yesh,</t>
    <t s="8">and the drawing down of the miracles is from the aspect of the essence of Chochmah that is above the source for Binah – the Ayin of true Yesh.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
